deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages). The page concerns the projective line minus three points, X = P^1 - {0,1,∞}, and its S_3 symmetry, which permutes the three punctures. Notation:
- π is the fundamental group of X, free of rank 2, generated by the loops l_0, l_1, l_∞ subject to the single relation l_∞ l_1 l_0 = 1.
- Σ is the extension 1 → π → Σ → S_3 → 1, the orbifold fundamental group of X/S_3.
- σ_0, σ_1, σ_∞ are lifts of the three transpositions, chosen to be involutions. σ_i fixes puncture i and swaps the other two.
- ρ is a lift of the 3-cycle, with ρ^3 = 1. It is fixed by a 'trivial path from P to P̄', P probably being a symmetric base point.
- Relations already established: σ_0σ_1 = ρ l_0, σ_1σ_∞ = ρ l_1, σ_∞σ_0 = ρ l_∞.
- int(σ_0) fixes the class of l_0 and swaps l_1 and l_∞: σ_0(l_1) = l_∞, σ_0(l_∞) = l_1, σ_0(l_0) = (l_1 l_∞)^{-1}, which is conjugate to l_0.
- int(ρ) permutes the loops cyclically: 0 → 1 → ∞ → 0.

In modern terms Σ ≅ ⟨σ_0, ρ | σ_0^2 = ρ^3 = 1⟩ ≅ Z/2 * Z/3 ≅ PSL_2(Z). π corresponds to Γ(2)/±1, the λ-line, and X/S_3 is the j-line.

This page. Grothendieck wants square roots of the puncture loops inside the extension (called E^+ here). He defines:
(8) ε_0 = l_0 σ_0 l_1, ε_1 = l_1 σ_1 l_∞, ε_∞ = l_∞ σ_∞ l_0.

These are the parabolic generators of the cusp stabilizers; ε_0 plays the role of T, with T^2 lying in Γ(2).
- He notes the cyclic equivariance ρ ε_i ρ^{-1} = ε_{ρ(i)}.
- He verifies ε_0^2 = l_0 · σ_0(l_1 l_0) · σ_0^2 · l_1 = l_0 l_1^{-1} l_1 = l_0, using σ_0(l_1 l_0) = l_∞ (l_1 l_∞)^{-1} = l_1^{-1}.

He then proposes a presentation of E^+ on generators l_0, l_1, l_∞, ε_0, ε_1, ε_∞, ρ, with relations:
- l_∞ l_1 l_0 = 1;
- ε_i^2 = l_i;
- ρ^3 = 1;
- ε_0ε_1 = ρ·(word in the l_i), and its cyclic analogues.

Computing the first of these:
ε_0ε_1 = l_0 (σ_0 l_1^2 σ_0^{-1})(σ_0σ_1) l_∞ = l_0 l_∞^2 ρ l_0 l_∞.

The cyclic analogues give
(9) ε_0ε_1 = l_0 l_∞^2 ρ l_0 l_∞, ε_1ε_∞ = l_1 l_0^2 ρ l_1 l_0, ε_∞ε_0 = l_∞ l_1^2 ρ l_∞ l_1.

The page ends by announcing that eliminating l_i = ε_i^2 yields a presentation on ε_0, ε_1, ε_∞, ρ. The next page redoes this with changed conventions (l_i replaced by l_i^{-1}) in the 'dessins' notation.

Purpose: an explicit S_3-equivariant presentation of the λ-line orbifold group and its cusp square roots. This is groundwork for the Galois action on π and on Σ, and for the cartographic-group / dessins setting of Printemps 81.
errors: No genuine error found: the ε_0^2 = l_0 check and formula (9) are correct, given σ_0^2 = 1, σ_0σ_1 = ρ l_0 and the stated action of σ_0.
Formula (9) is not simplified: l_0 l_∞ = l_1^{-1}, so ε_0ε_1 = l_0 l_∞^2 ρ l_1^{-1}, and cyclically.

The proposed presentation is left incomplete. The final elimination is only announced, and the next page changes the conventions (l_i → l_i^{-1}, different σ indices), so the formulas in (8) are not final.

Previous-page notation σ_0(l_0) = l_0^{-1}l_1^{-1} differs from this page's (l_1 l_∞)^{-1}. Only the latter is consistent with σ_0 being an automorphism that swaps l_1 and l_∞; the convention shift is acknowledged on the next page.

ideas.what: Extension of π_1(P^1-{0,1,∞}) by S_3, with involutive lifts σ_i and an order-3 lift ρ.
ideas.modern_name: Orbifold fundamental group of the λ-line modulo S_3 ≅ PSL_2(Z) ≅ Z/2*Z/3; Γ(2)/±1 ⊂ PSL_2(Z)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Klein, Fricke); Galois-theoretic use by Ihara and Nakamura in the 1980s-90s
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984): cartographic groups, PSL_2(Z) and the Galois action; explicit formulas unsure

ideas.what: Square roots ε_i of the puncture loops l_i inside the S_3-extension, with ρ-equivariance and products ε_iε_j expressed as ρ times words in the l_i.
ideas.modern_name: Parabolic (cusp) generators T with T^2 in Γ(2); presentation of PSL_2(Z) via cusp generators

ideas.what: Using the S_3 symmetry of the three-punctured line to constrain Galois/outer automorphisms through explicit lifts of transpositions and of the 3-cycle.
ideas.modern_name: Source of the 2-cycle and 3-cycle (hexagon) relations in the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, programme only; no formulas)

missed.claim: In 1981 Grothendieck explicitly computes, in the S_3-extension of π_1(P^1-{0,1,∞}), lifts of the 2- and 3-cycles (σ_i, ρ) and the relations σ_0σ_1 = ρl_0, etc. Requiring a Galois automorphism to respect these lifts is exactly what produces the GT 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations later written by Drinfeld and Ihara. The page documents the group-theoretic groundwork, though it does not state those relations.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it gives a concrete early trace of the S_3 symmetry computations that underlie GT, predating Drinfeld. It is not a new mathematical result.

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine explicit computations in PSL_2(Z) ≅ Z/2*Z/3 / the λ-line orbifold group. Their historical interest is as early 1981 groundwork for the S_3/GT-type relations; nothing on the page is mathematically new.
transcription_corrections: In (8) the l's carry small superscript marks (asterisk-like). These are probably later annotations signalling the l_i → l_i^{-1} change of convention made on the next page; they are not part of the formulas.
In the system of relations, 'ε_0ε_1 = ρ(...)' appears in the image as ρ followed by a struck-through argument, possibly 'ρ(l_1)'.
'Ici {+on E^+ +} donc qu'on a une syst. de gén. et relations' is more plausibly 'Ici on a (dans E^+) donc qu'on a un syst. de gén. et relations'.
The final line plausibly reads 'Éliminant les l_i comme ε_i^2, on trouve des gén. ε_0, ε_1, ε_∞, ρ, une relation de définition...' (the sentence continues on the next page).
